duolingo-full.title: Duolingo English Test — Full Strategy
duolingo-full.summary: Master the adaptive Duolingo English Test (DET) with question-by-question strategies, timing tactics, and proven techniques to score 120+ on the 10–160 scale.

slides.title: What Is The Duolingo English Test?
points: Online English proficiency exam, ~1 hour duration, taken from home
Adaptive: difficulty scales up/down based on your answers
AI-proctored + occasional human review; strict rules (no looking away, no notes, one face)
Cost: ~$65 USD; results delivered in 48 hours
Accepted by 4,000+ universities and institutions worldwide

example.label: Test Flow
example.text: Take exam at home → Duolingo system grades + flags for review → Human proctor spot-checks → Score arrives in 2 days

slides.tip: Book your test slot online; ensure quiet room, stable internet, and webcam visible to AI.
slides.warn: Late arrival or proctoring violations result in cancellation and fee forfeiture.

slides.title: DET Scoring: 10–160 Scale + 4 Subscores
points: Overall score: 10–160 (reported every 5 points: 10, 15, 20, etc.)
Literacy (reading accuracy): measures spelling, grammar recognition
Comprehension (listening/reading understanding): vocabulary, detail recall
Conversation (dialogue flow, turn-taking): naturalness and responsiveness
Production (speaking/writing quality): clarity, fluency, structure

example.label: Sample Report
example.text: Total: 130 | Literacy: 135 | Comprehension: 128 | Conversation: 125 | Production: 130

slides.tip: Universities usually want 100+; competitive schools prefer 120+. Check each school's DET requirement.
slides.warn: Low Conversation or Production scores flag language poverty; practise real dialogue, not robotic speech.

slides.title: Test Structure & Timing
points: Total: ~45–60 minutes (adaptive; harder path = longer)
20–25 task items across 14 question types (mix of reading, listening, speaking, writing)
No breaks; AI watches the whole time
Easier items first; difficulty jumps if you answer correctly
Each item takes 1–4 minutes (varies by type)

example.label: Typical Session
example.text: Read and Complete (2 min) → Read Aloud (1 min) → Listen and Type (2 min) → Write About Photo (3 min) → ... → Speaking/Writing samples (5 min each)

slides.tip: Pace yourself: spend 1–2 min per short task, 3–4 min per long ones. Don't freeze on hard items.
slides.warn: Running out of time on the final speaking/writing sample hurts your Production score heavily.

slides.title: Read and Complete (C-Test)
points: 5–7 sentences; every few words replaced with a blank
Choose from 2–3 word options per blank
Tests grammar, vocabulary, collocation
Usually the easiest question type; Literacy score driver

example.label: Sample
example.text: The meeting was __1__ (cancelled/postponed) due to ___2___ (weather/rain). All attendees were __3__ (notified/aware) via email.

slides.tip: Eliminate wrong words (verb tense, gender, part of speech). Read the full sentence context before choosing.
slides.warn: Don't guess randomly; use grammar rules (tense consistency, word order) to narrow options.

slides.title: Read Aloud
points: Read a 1–2 sentence passage aloud; AI grades pronunciation, intonation, fluency
40–60 seconds to speak
Production score driver; major impression point
Accent: less important than clarity and confidence

example.label: Sample Prompt
example.text: A good leader listens to their team and adapts strategies based on feedback.

slides.tip: Speak clearly and naturally; don't rush or monotone. Pause between sentences. Make eye contact with webcam.
slides.warn: Mumbling, extreme speed, or lack of confidence tanks the score even if words are correct.

slides.title: Listen and Type (Dictation)
points: Audio clip (1–2 sentences); you type what you hear
30–60 second clip; play once or twice
Comprehension + Literacy test (spelling, word recognition)
Accent varies (American, British, Indian accents common)

example.label: Sample Audio
example.text: [Female US voice] The quarterly report highlighted a twenty-five percent increase in customer satisfaction.

slides.tip: Listen for whole phrases, not word-by-word. Capitalize proper nouns. Don't overthink spelling.
slides.warn: Missing a word or misspelling hurts the Literacy score; listen a second time if unsure.

slides.title: Write About the Photo
points: Image shown; you write 1–2 sentences describing it
Open-ended; graded on grammar, vocabulary, relevance
30–90 seconds to write
Production score driver

example.label: Sample Prompt
example.text: [Image of a crowded market] Describe what you see in the photo.

slides.tip: Describe objects, actions, colors, mood. Use compound sentences (and, but, because). Aim for 2 well-formed sentences.
slides.warn: One-word answers or irrelevant text score zero. Spelling matters; grammar must be correct.

slides.title: Read and Select (Fake Word Detection)
points: 4–5 words shown; 1 is NOT a real English word
You select the fake word
Tests vocabulary and word recognition
Literacy score contributor

example.label: Sample
example.text: A) flourish  B) fleeced  C) fluminate  D) flinch | Answer: C (not a real word)

slides.tip: Sound out unfamiliar words. Most are real; only one is fake. Don't overthink.
slides.warn: Confusing English with other languages (e.g., French -ment endings) leads to wrong guesses.

slides.title: Listen and Select (Multiple Choice Listening)
points: Audio clip (20–40 seconds); answer multiple-choice question
4–5 answer options; 1–2 correct details hidden in the clip
Comprehension score driver
Distractors include similar-sounding wrong answers

example.label: Sample Prompt
example.text: Audio: [Person talks about moving to Berlin for a job] | Q: Why did the person move? A) Job B) School C) Family D) Travel

slides.tip: Focus on key facts (who, what, when, why). Ignore minor details. Re-listen if you miss the answer.
slides.warn: Accent and speed can hide the answer; don't panic if you don't catch every word.

slides.title: Speak About the Photo
points: Image shown; you speak for 40–60 seconds describing it
Graded on pronunciation, grammar, vocabulary, fluency
Major Production score contributor
Conversation and Production both affected

example.label: Sample Prompt
example.text: [Image of a family cooking together] Describe what's happening in this photo.

slides.tip: Describe setting, people, actions, emotions. Use complete sentences. Pause naturally; don't rush.
slides.warn: Silence or filler sounds (um, uh) too often lowers the fluency score significantly.

slides.title: Read Then Speak
points: Read a 1–2 sentence prompt; then speak your response (40–60 seconds)
Example: 'What do you do to stay healthy?' or 'Describe your ideal vacation.'
Production + Conversation scores both tested
Requires preparation time (~20 seconds) before you speak

example.label: Sample Prompt
example.text: Question: If you could travel anywhere, where would it be and why? | You respond: I would go to Japan because I love the culture and food...

slides.tip: Plan briefly (use the prep time). Structure: introduction + 2–3 reasons + conclusion. Speak naturally.
slides.warn: Rambling without structure or excessive hesitation reduces the fluency and coherence scores.

slides.title: Listen Then Speak
points: Listen to a question (20–40 seconds); then answer it out loud (40–60 seconds)
Tests comprehension + ability to respond spontaneously
Conversation score driver (turn-taking simulation)
Accent and naturalness matter

example.label: Sample
example.text: Audio question: 'What's your opinion on remote work?' | You respond: I think remote work has many advantages, like flexibility, but it can also feel isolating.

slides.tip: Listen for the key question. Answer directly; don't repeat the question. Use complete sentences.
slides.warn: Misunderstanding the question and answering off-topic scores very low on Comprehension.

slides.title: Writing Sample (Essay)
points: Prompt given (e.g., 'Describe your biggest achievement'); you write for 3–5 minutes
150–300 words expected; graded on grammar, vocabulary, organization, relevance
Production score driver; major impact on final score
One chance; no editing after submission

example.label: Sample Prompt
example.text: Describe a time you overcame a challenge. What was it? How did you handle it? What did you learn?

slides.tip: Outline first: intro (1 sentence) + body (2–3 reasons/examples) + conclusion (1 sentence). Use topic sentences.
slides.warn: Spelling and grammar errors accumulate; aim for zero critical errors. Don't ramble off-topic.

slides.title: Speaking Sample (Monologue)
points: Prompt given (e.g., 'Tell us about your family'); you speak for 1–2 minutes
Graded on pronunciation, grammar, vocabulary, fluency, coherence
Major Production + Conversation score contributor
Naturalness and confidence heavily weighted

example.label: Sample Prompt
example.text: Describe your ideal job. What would you do? Why appeals to you? What skills would you need?

slides.tip: Speak naturally; pauses are OK. Structure: intro → body (2–3 points) → conclusion. Make eye contact with webcam.
slides.warn: Sounding robotic, scripted, or overly formal reduces the Conversation score even if grammar is perfect.

slides.title: Interactive Reading
points: Longer passage (3–5 paragraphs); multiple-choice or fill-in-blank questions
Tests comprehension of main idea, details, inference
Comprehension score driver
Adaptive: harder passages if you answer correctly

example.label: Sample Passage
example.text: A 3-paragraph article on renewable energy; questions ask about main idea, specific facts, or author's intent.

slides.tip: Skim the passage first; focus on topic sentences. Look for keyword matches between question and text.
slides.warn: Don't overthink implied meanings; answers are usually explicit in the passage.

slides.title: Interactive Listening
points: Longer audio clip (1–2 minutes, e.g., lecture, podcast, conversation); multiple-choice questions
Tests comprehension of main idea, details, speaker intent
Comprehension score driver
Various accents and speaking speeds common

example.label: Sample Audio
example.text: A 90-second podcast on productivity tips; 4–5 questions about key points.

slides.tip: Take notes on key ideas. Listen for signal words (first, next, however, in conclusion). Don't focus on every word.
slides.warn: Speed and accent vary widely; focus on comprehension, not perfect word-for-word understanding.

slides.title: Summarize the Conversation
points: Listen to a 2–3 minute dialogue (2 speakers); then summarize it in 1–2 minutes of speech
Tests comprehension + spoken summarization ability
Conversation + Production + Comprehension all scored
Requires you to identify key points and omit details

example.label: Sample Dialogue
example.text: [Person A asks Person B about their new job] | You summarize: The dialogue is about [Person B]'s new job. [They] mentioned the role involves [X], and [they] felt [emotion] about the transition.

slides.tip: Identify the main topic (who, what). List 2–3 key points. Speak clearly and organized.
slides.warn: Repeating every detail makes your summary too long; focus on the main idea and 1–2 supporting facts.

slides.title: Proctoring Rules (AI + Human)
points: Webcam must show your face and upper body the entire test
Don't look away, leave the frame, or look at other screens
No notes, books, earbuds, or second monitor visible
Solo room; no one else can be present
One face per test; multiple people = automatic cancellation

example.label: Setup Check
example.text: Quiet room, good lighting, webcam at eye level, desk clear except keyboard/mouse, internet stable.

slides.tip: Test your setup 24 hours before. Do a practice test to ensure AI recognizes your face.
slides.warn: Frequent pausing, looking away, or suspicious background activity flags you for human review or cancellation.

slides.title: Timing Strategy: What To Rush & What To Slow Down
points: Spend 1–2 min per short task (Read and Complete, Read Aloud, Listen and Type)
Spend 2–3 min per medium task (Listen and Select, Speak About Photo, Read Then Speak)
Spend 3–5 min per long task (Writing/Speaking Sample, Interactive tasks)
Leave 2 min buffer for unexpected delays

example.label: 60-Min Test Allocation
example.text: Short tasks (10 min) → Medium tasks (15 min) → Long tasks (30 min) → Buffer (5 min)

slides.tip: If a task is hard, skip it mentally and move forward; come back if time allows. Don't lose time on one item.
slides.warn: Running out of time on the writing/speaking sample tanks your Production score heavily; prioritize those.

slides.title: Top Mistakes & How To Avoid Them
points: Guessing randomly on Read and Select or Listen and Select: use logic and word recognition instead.
Speaking too fast on Read Aloud and Speak About Photo: clarity and confidence beat speed.
Writing short, choppy sentences on Writing Sample: use compound/complex sentences to show grammar.
Misunderstanding questions on Listen Then Speak: ask yourself the question in your mind before answering.

example.label: Common Error
example.text: Student rushes through Listen and Type, misses 3 words → spelling/comprehension score drops. Fix: replay audio twice.

slides.tip: Review your own speaking/writing before submitting; catch obvious grammar errors or incomplete sentences.
slides.warn: Over-relying on scripted answers on spontaneous tasks (Listen Then Speak) sounds unnatural and scores lower.

slides.title: Writing Sample: Structure & Grammar Checklist
points: Outline: intro (state main point) → body (2–3 reasons or examples) → conclusion (restate + broader thought)
Grammar: subject-verb agreement, consistent tense, no sentence fragments, correct punctuation
Vocabulary: use varied words; avoid repeating the same adjective (good, good, good = bad)
Length: 150–300 words; don't pad with irrelevant sentences

example.label: Good Intro
example.text: One of my biggest achievements was earning my degree while working full-time. This required discipline, time management, and support from family.

slides.tip: Use transition words (first, next, however, in conclusion) to link ideas. End with a strong conclusion that reflects on the lesson learned.
slides.warn: Repetitive or circular writing (saying the same thing twice) wastes words and suggests low English level.

slides.title: Speaking Sample: Fluency & Naturalness
points: Speak at natural pace; don't rush or drag. Pauses between thoughts are normal.
Use contractions (I'm, that's, don't) like a native speaker; don't sound stiff
Vary sentence structure: simple, compound, complex sentences all mixed
Emphasize key words naturally; avoid robotic monotone
Filler sounds (um, uh, like) hurt fluency; silence is better than filler

example.label: Good vs. Bad
example.text: Good: 'I would go to Japan because, um, I love the food and culture. The temples are amazing.' Bad: 'I like Japan. It is good. Japan has food. I like food.'

slides.tip: Record yourself speaking the same prompt 3 times; pick the most natural take for your final answer.
slides.warn: Sounding like you're reading a script (flat intonation, perfect but robotic) scores lower than slightly imperfect but natural speech.

slides.title: Read Aloud: Pronunciation & Confidence Tips
points: Pronounce unfamiliar words phonetically; don't guess wildly
Use natural intonation: rise at end of questions, fall at end of statements
Stress correct syllables (proNOUNCE, not PROnouce); check a dictionary if unsure
Smile while speaking; it comes through in your tone even over audio
Speak loudly enough to be clearly heard; don't whisper

example.label: Word Stress Matters
example.text: RECORD (noun, RECord) vs. reCORD (verb, reKORD) — wrong stress changes meaning.

slides.tip: If you mispronounce a word, keep going naturally; don't stop and correct yourself.
slides.warn: Extreme accent or unintelligible words (even if grammatically correct) lower Production score; clarity is key.

slides.title: Interactive Reading: Main Idea vs. Detail Questions
points: Main idea: 'What is the passage mostly about?' — pick the broadest, most general answer
Detail: 'According to the passage, what did X do?' — find exact words or paraphrase in text
Inference: 'What can you infer about X?' — answer must be supported by the passage, not outside knowledge
Wrong answers (distractors): often include true facts from the passage but don't answer the question

example.label: Main Idea Example
example.text: Passage about solar energy benefits. Q: Main idea? A) Solar panels are made of silicon (detail, not main) → Wrong. A) Solar energy is a renewable alternative to fossil fuels (main) → Correct.

slides.tip: For detail questions, search the text for keyword matches. Don't use outside knowledge.
slides.warn: Picking a true statement that doesn't answer the question is a common trap.

slides.title: Interactive Listening: Note-Taking Technique
points: Don't write full sentences; use abbreviations (BC = because, → = leads to, + = and, w/ = with)
Focus on WHO, WHAT, WHEN, WHERE, WHY for main idea questions
Underline or star key numbers, names, or contradictions
Leave blank lines for points you miss; keep listening rather than stopping

example.label: Sample Notes
example.text: Speaker A: needs new job → low salary. Speaker B: suggests startup → high risk but growth. Decision: A considers it.

slides.tip: Review your notes immediately after listening; circle the answer to each question based on your notes.
slides.warn: Over-writing causes you to miss the next sentence; balance note-taking with active listening.

slides.title: Adaptive Difficulty Strategy
points: Early questions are easy: answer carefully but don't over-think; correct answers unlock harder material
Harder questions give you more points: don't panic if they seem impossible; even 1–2 correct helps
Adaptive direction: correct → harder next, incorrect → easier next. This balances your ceiling.
Your score depends on the hardest items you got right, not the total number correct

example.label: Adaptive Path
example.text: Q1 Easy ✓ → Q2 Harder ✓ → Q3 Hard ✓ → Q4 Very Hard ✗ → Q5 Hard (different topic) ✓ → Final score based on max difficulty reached.

slides.tip: Don't celebrate early correct answers or feel defeated by wrong ones; focus on your next question.
slides.warn: Skipping or rushing early items costs points; the easier questions still contribute to your overall score.

slides.title: Test Day Checklist (24 Hours Before)
points: Internet speed: test your connection (5+ Mbps download/upload minimum)
Webcam & microphone: test both; ensure they're not covered by stickers or reflections
Room lighting: bright and even; no harsh shadows on your face
Background: clear, plain wall behind you; no visible chaos or distractions
Audio: close other tabs, silence phone, ask housemates not to make noise

example.label: Quick Test
example.text: Run a free Duolingo English Test practice; verify the proctoring AI can see your face clearly and mic picks up your voice.

slides.tip: Do a full dry run of the exam software 24 hours before; fix tech issues early.
slides.warn: Discovering webcam or internet problems during the test = cancellation and lost fee.

slides.title: Worked Example: Full Question Flow
points: Scenario: You're on Q11 of 22. Medium difficulty, no pattern yet.
Task type: Listen Then Speak. Audio asks: 'What's your favourite subject and why?'
Your approach: Listen once (1 min), jot 'fav subject = biology, why = patient, hands-on'
Response: 'My favourite subject is biology. I like it because it's hands-on and teaches me how living things work.' (45 sec)
Grade: clear, natural, on-topic → Comprehension and Conversation both score +. Harder Q12 next.

example.label: Q12 (Harder)
example.text: Summarize the Conversation: 2-min dialogue about choosing a career. You summarize in 90 seconds.

slides.tip: This example shows the adaptive flow; each correct answer raises the bar, but the structure and strategy stay the same.
slides.warn: If Q12 is too hard, your next item might drop back to medium; this is normal and helps calibrate your score.

slides.title: After The Test: What To Expect
points: AI-generated score sent within 2 hours (provisional; may update after human review)
Human proctor reviews 2–5% of tests randomly; most scores final after 24 hours
If flagged for unusual patterns (e.g., perfect speaking sample + poor writing), human may adjust score
Score report includes overall + 4 subscores; sent via email and DET portal
University access: you choose which schools get your score (free send to 5 schools)

example.label: Timeline
example.text: 12:30 pm: Finish test → 1:00 pm: AI score arrives → 2:00 pm–48 hrs: Human review possible → Score finalized.

slides.tip: If your score is lower than expected, Duolingo allows retakes; data shows second attempts often improve Conversation and Production.
slides.warn: Scores are valid for 2 years. Don't wait too long to submit to universities.

slides.title: Next Steps: Free Duolingo Mocks & Practice
points: Take 2–3 free DET practice tests on Duolingo's website (simulates full adaptive experience)
Record yourself on each speaking task; compare to good models (YouTube has DET tutorials)
Write 5–10 sample essays on common prompts (travel, achievement, career, learning, relationships)
Listen to TED talks and podcasts at 1.5x speed to build comprehension stamina
Join DET study groups (Reddit, Discord) to hear others' speaking samples and get feedback

example.label: 7-Day Prep Plan
example.text: Day 1–2: Full mock + review | Day 3–4: Task-type drills + speaking recordings | Day 5–6: Writing samples + listening practice | Day 7: Final mock + rest.

slides.tip: Duolingo offers free practice tests (not full official tests) on their prep portal; use them to identify weak areas.
slides.warn: Official paid test is different from free practice; expect real test to feel harder. But strategies here apply to both.

slides.title: Final Mindset: DET Success Principles
points: Adaptive = no fixed 'hard' or 'easy'; your goal is to answer thoughtfully at your current level
Natural > Perfect: sounding like a native speaker who sometimes hesitates beats flawless robot speech
Time management > Perfection: finish all sections even if some answers are rushed; partial credit beats skipped sections
Confidence shows: clear voice, steady pace, eye contact with webcam matter as much as words
Practice with real tasks: Duolingo mocks are your best friends; don't just read about the test

example.label: Scoring Mindset
example.text: A 125 is not 'perfect English' — it's conversational competence + strong grammar + minor mistakes accepted. Aim for 120+, celebrate 110+.

slides.tip: On test day, treat the AI proctor like a friendly conversation partner, not a judge. Relax, speak clearly, and trust your prep.
slides.warn: Overthinking during the test (e.g., worrying about accent) causes stumbling and lowers fluency; stay focused on the task.
